# Neo-Confucianism quotes

Neo-Confucianism renews Confucian ethics through metaphysics of principle and heart-mind, shaping East Asian education and moral practice.

20 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Zhu Xi systematizes li and qi; Wang Yangming emphasizes the unity of knowledge and action and innate moral knowing. The archive’s passages stress cultivation, sincerity, and practical learning.

## Historical notes

Song–Ming Neo-Confucianism responds to Buddhist and Daoist challenges while reclaiming Confucian classics as living moral psychology.

## Core ideas

-   Principle (li) structures both cosmos and ethics.
-   Self-cultivation is intellectual and practical.
-   Knowledge and action should not be split (Wang Yangming).
-   Sincerity and investigation of things form a paired discipline.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Zhang Zai](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhang-zai) , [Zhu Xi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhu-xi) , [Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) , [Wang Fuzhi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-fuzhi)

## FAQ

### What is Neo-Confucianism?

It is the Song–Ming renewal of Confucian thought with a richer metaphysics and a focus on moral self-cultivation.

### How does it differ from classical Confucianism?

It keeps humaneness and ritual central while developing systematic accounts of principle, heart-mind, and practice.
